title: Immersion comparison for projective-bundle line quotients
statement: Let $g:Z\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and let $N$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Suppose $q:g^*F\twoheadrightarrow N$ is a surjective sheaf homomorphism, and let $r:Z\to\mathbf P_X(F)$ be its classifying morphism over $X$, using tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] and the tautological quotient and classification of [def-per-projective-bundle-quotient-data, lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry]. Let $(V_j)_{j\in J}$ be an open covering of $X$, put $Z_j=g^{-1}(V_j)$ and $g_j=g|_{Z_j}$, and suppose there are quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{V_j}$-modules $E_j$ and maps $\alpha_j:E_j\to F|_{V_j}$ such that $q_j=q|_{Z_j}\circ g_j^*\alpha_j$ is surjective and its classifying map $i_j:Z_j\to\mathbf P_{V_j}(E_j)$ is an immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $P_j=\mathbf P_{V_j}(F|_{V_j})$ with projection $p_j$. Let $U_j$ be the subset of $P_j$ where the composite $p_j^*E_j\xrightarrow{p_j^*\alpha_j}p_j^*(F|_{V_j})\to\mathcal O_{P_j}(1)$ is surjective on stalks. Then $U_j$ is open, the quotient on $U_j$ classifies a morphism $h_j:U_j\to\mathbf P_{V_j}(E_j)$, and $r|_{Z_j}$ factors through $\widetilde r_j:Z_j\to U_j$ with $h_j\circ\widetilde r_j=i_j$. In particular $r$ is an immersion. There is no quasi-compactness or finite-type hypothesis on $g$, $E_j$ or $F$.

source.place: Tag 01VR (lemma-relatively-very-ample), proof (2) implies (4), comparison open U_j, omitted verification of the factorization, and immersion conclusion; formulated for an arbitrary quotient q, independent of its evaluation origin.

proof.text: Put $P=\mathbf P_X(F)$ and let $p:P\to X$ be its projection. By [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry], $p^{-1}(V_j)$ with its quotient is $P_j$, these opens cover $P$, and the restriction $r_j:Z_j\to P_j$ classifies $q|_{Z_j}$. In particular there is a quotient-compatible isomorphism $r_j^*\mathcal O_{P_j}(1)\simeq N|_{Z_j}$. Write $Q_j=\mathcal O_{P_j}(1)$ and $\beta_j:p_j^*E_j\to Q_j$ for the composite in the statement. Functoriality of tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] and this isomorphism identify $r_j^*\beta_j$ with $q_j$.

source.place: Tag 01VR (lemma-relatively-very-ample), proof (2) implies (4), comparison open and omitted factorization verification; using Constructions Tags 01OA/01OB for quotient classification.

proof.text: We check openness directly, without a finiteness hypothesis on the source of $\beta_j$. For $y\in U_j$, trivialize $Q_j$ near $y$ with frame $l$, using [def-sc-invertible-module]. Surjectivity at $y$ gives a germ $e_y$ with $\beta_{j,y}(e_y)=l_y$. Represent $e_y$ by a section $e$ on a smaller neighbourhood and shrink once more so that $\beta_j(e)=l$ there. On that neighbourhood the map $a l\mapsto a e$ is a right inverse to $\beta_j$, so every point lies in $U_j$. Thus $U_j$ is open; $\beta_j|_{U_j}$ is surjective as a sheaf map by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-surjective-iff-stalks].

source.place: Tag 01VR (lemma-relatively-very-ample), proof (2) implies (4), comparison open and omitted factorization verification; using Constructions Tags 01OA/01OB for quotient classification.

proof.text: Apply the quotient classification of [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry] over $V_j$ to the invertible quotient $\beta_j|_{U_j}:(p_j|_{U_j})^*E_j\twoheadrightarrow Q_j|_{U_j}$. It gives a morphism $h_j:U_j\to\mathbf P_{V_j}(E_j)$ over $V_j$ and a quotient-compatible identification of its pulled tautological quotient with $\beta_j|_{U_j}$.

source.place: Tag 01VR (lemma-relatively-very-ample), proof (2) implies (4), comparison open and omitted factorization verification; using Constructions Tags 01OA/01OB for quotient classification.

proof.text: For $z\in Z_j$ put $y=r_j(z)$, $A=\mathcal O_{P_j,y}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{Z_j,z}$. The stalk homomorphism $A\to B$ is local [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback], naturally in the module, $(r_j^*\beta_j)_z$ is $\beta_{j,y}\otimes_A B$. If $y\notin U_j$, choose a frame $Q_{j,y}\simeq A$. The image of $\beta_{j,y}$ is a proper ideal $I\subset A$, hence $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$: an element outside $\mathfrak m_A$ is a unit and would make $I=A$. Every image of a pure tensor under $\beta_{j,y}\otimes_A B$ then lies in $\mathfrak m_AB\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$, and finite sums do too. Thus this tensor map cannot hit $1\in B$. But step 1 identifies it with the surjective stalk map $(q_j)_z$; stalk surjectivity follows from [lem-weil-pbc-locally-surjective-iff-stalks]. This contradiction proves $r_j(Z_j)\subseteq U_j$.

source.place: Tag 01VR (lemma-relatively-very-ample), proof (2) implies (4), comparison open and omitted factorization verification; using Constructions Tags 01OA/01OB for quotient classification.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme], the inclusion just proved gives a unique $\widetilde r_j:Z_j\to U_j$ with composite $r_j$. Pull back the quotient classified by $h_j$ along $\widetilde r_j$. By the arbitrary-pullback naturality of [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry], $h_j\circ\widetilde r_j$ classifies $r_j^*\beta_j$, which is $q_j$ under the quotient-compatible isomorphism of step 1. The given $i_j$ classifies the same quotient. Injectivity of that classification bijection therefore gives $h_j\circ\widetilde r_j=i_j$.

source.place: Tag 01VR (lemma-relatively-very-ample), proof (2) implies (4), comparison open and omitted factorization verification; using Constructions Tags 01OA/01OB for quotient classification.

proof.text: Since $h_j\circ\widetilde r_j=i_j$ is an immersion, [lem-zl-immersion-cancellation] implies that $\widetilde r_j$ is an immersion. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], factor it as a closed immersion into an open subscheme $W_j\subset U_j$, followed by the inclusion. The set $W_j$ is also open in $P_j$, and its structure sheaf is the restriction of that of $P_j$: restriction through two nested opens is restriction to the smaller open [def-weil-open-immersion]. The same closed immersion followed by $W_j\hookrightarrow P_j$ is $r_j$, so $r_j$ is an immersion. The opens $P_j\subset P$ cover $P$, and $r^{-1}(P_j)=Z_j$. Apply [lem-zl-immersion-near-image-locality] to this cover to conclude that $r$ is an immersion.

lean.note: The auxiliary maps are explicit composites of the recorded section-normalized tensor pullbacks. HasQuotientOpenComparison unfolds to the exact open-locus and classifying factorization conclusions over one base open, including the quotient-compatible base restriction identification. No finiteness, quasi-compactness or local freeness of F or E is assumed.
